questions.q:
Give the time signature for:
(a) three crotchet beats in a bar
(b) two dotted-crotchet beats in a bar
questions.tip: Compound time: each beat is a dotted note, divided into three quavers.

questions.q: Put these tempo markings in order from slowest to fastest: allegro, largo, presto, andante.
ms: largo slowest, then andante (both in the correct place)
allegro then presto (fastest) in the correct place

questions.q:
Which single note value completes each bar?
(a) 4/4: minim, crotchet, quaver, ?
(b) 3/4: dotted crotchet, ?
(c) 6/8: crotchet, quaver, ?
(d) 2/4: quaver, semiquaver, semiquaver, ?
questions.model: (a) quaver (b) dotted crotchet (c) dotted crotchet (d) crotchet
questions.tip: Add up in crotchet beats: e.g. 6/8 = 3 crotchets' worth; crotchet + quaver = 1.5, so 1.5 more.

questions.q:
Name the rhythmic or tempo feature described.
(a) In a minuet in 3/4, the two bars before the cadence are accented as if they were one bar of 3/2.
(b) A song starts with one quaver before the first bar line.
(c) Accents fall on the off-beats, with notes tied across the beat.
(d) The music gradually gets faster.

In 4/4, a forward (3–2) son clave has hits on: bar 1 – beat 1, the 'and' of beat 2, beat 4; bar 2 – beats 2 and 3.
(a) How many hits are there in one complete clave pattern? [1]
(b) How would the reverse (2–3) clave start? [1]
(c) Explain why the clave is a cross-rhythm against the beat. [2]
(d) On what instrument is the clave pattern traditionally played? [1]
(e) Teental is a Hindustani tāla. How many beats does its cycle have? [1]
ms: (b) with the two-hit bar (beats 2 and 3) first, then the three-hit bar
(c) some hits fall off the main beats (e.g. the 'and' of 2)
(c) the uneven grouping (3 + 3 + 2 quavers' feel in bar 1) conflicts with the steady four-beat pulse
questions.model: (a) Five. (b) It starts with the two-hit bar (beats 2 and 3). (c) The hit on the 'and' of beat 2 falls between beats, so the 3-hit bar is grouped unevenly against the steady four-beat pulse, creating a cross-rhythm. (d) Claves. (e) 16 beats.
questions.tip: All the other salsa parts fit around the clave, so it is called the rhythmic 'key'.

questions.q:
A passage in 3/4 is marked ♩ = 120.
(a) How long does one bar last, in seconds? [1]
(b) How long do 16 bars last? [1]
(c) The last two bars are marked 'rit.' and 'dim.', ending on 'pp' with a pause sign. Explain what the performer does. [3]
(d) The next section is marked 'a tempo' and begins with 'sf'. Explain these markings. [2]
ms: (a) 120 beats per minute = 2 beats per second, so 3 beats = 1.5 seconds
(c) dim. – gradually gets quieter, ending pianissimo / very quietly
(c) pause – holds the final note longer than written
(d) a tempo – return to the original speed (♩ = 120)
(d) sf (sforzando) – a sudden strong accent on that note
questions.model: (a) 1.5 seconds (2 beats per second, 3 beats per bar). (b) 24 seconds. (c) The performer gradually slows down and gets quieter, ending very quietly and holding the last note longer than its value. (d) a tempo: go back to the original speed; sf: play the first note with a sudden strong accent.
questions.tip: Show the working for timing questions: beats per second first, then per bar.
